features.name: Attract scores: one timed HIGH SCORES screen of records' top entries between cabinet demos
Bar lines: a faint line and the bar number at each bar start, like Synthesia
Bar loop: practice bars X to Y at a slower tempo
Beat track: a drum beat on the piano under every song, so players can hear the time
Black-key lanes: the lanes under black keys shaded a little lighter, like Synthesia
Build stamp: the short commit and its age in a corner of /, so a stale build is obvious
Cabinet: a kiosk loop with a title screen, attract mode and a demo game
Calibration: tap along to clicks to set the latency offset
Capture mode: ?capture=1 hides the cursor, debug text and setup controls while the video is recorded
PROVISIONAL (learning lane): chart compiler from public-domain scores
Chart lint: a hand-span rule in the library test, every rule pinned by a synthetic chart, and a library table
Chord sync: flag chords rolled by more than 30 ms
Chunk practice: learn a song 4 bars at a time, then play each chunk judged at 70%
CI browser checks: the headless checks run on GitHub's machines, not Eric's Mac
Clear card: ALL PERFECT, FULL COMBO or CLEAR before the results
PROVISIONAL (learning lane): AI coach reads your takes and gives one drill
Combo in the HUD: the combo moves off the lanes into the panel's center
Play Twinkle on the real piano, judged, with a results screen
Crash guard: one plugin's error never freezes the game; a render error shows a card with a way back
Demo reset: Shift+Esc, or 60 s idle on a plain take's results, returns to / clean between judges
Difficulty: a level from 1 to 15 computed from each chart, shown and sorted in song select
Dynamics: grade how loud you played against the score
Easy charts: every song gets an Easy level derived from its chart, picked with E on the select
Evenness: score how even your runs are, per hand
Fever gauge: fever reachable on every song, scaled to its length
Fever moment: fever's start, loud at the edges for at most 2 s
Fever stage: a three.js synthwave stage behind the highway that reacts to your play
Spike: can webcam hand tracking tell which finger pressed a key?
First run: a 30-second guided Twinkle with laptop letters and text cues, one link and F away on /
Ghost: your last take drawn on the highway when you retry
Hand colors: left and right hands in two colors
Hand mode: play one hand while the DGX plays the other
Help overlay: ? shows every control on one card, and a test fails when a key handler has no help line
Hero replay: a downloaded take file drives /play, judged and sounding, the same every run
Highway zoom: the visible key range follows the music
Hit line: the animated electric judgment line
How it works: a /how page explaining how the agents built Piano Arcade, from real data
Arcade HUD with a giant combo, counters, score and multiplier
HUD skin: the HUD restyled to the tokens
Spike: can an iPad on the same wifi follow the sheet window?
Judging tiers: a GOOD tier that keeps the combo, early/late labels, and wrong notes that break it
Event sounds: count-in, combo stingers, fever, full combo, rank
Visual juice: wisps, bursts, lane light, fever, full combo and rank reveal
Key preview: a key glows faintly in its hand color for 500 ms before its note reaches the line
Key skin: the drawn keyboard with sheen and a pressed glow
Laptop octaves: Z and X shift the laptop keys an octave, and the keyboard shows the keys they play
Learn from the music select: L opens the focused song in wait mode
Learn progress: chunks cleared of total and the last practice date on the music select
Desktop learning frontend with four focused activities
LED game link: the game lights the next key and every hit on the strip
LED strip: the keys light up from the board, with a standalone tester
Left hands: the Minuet in G gets its left hand from its cited source; Twinkle's sources have none
Spike: can an acoustic piano play the game through the laptop microphone?
MIDI watchdog: reconnect when Chrome's input goes silent
Minuet in G: a second song, right hand, charted from a cited score
Note labels: letter names on notes and keys, laptop letters in laptop mode
Note pills: Synthesia-style notes, bright as they near the line
Notice toast: one styled stack for the game's notices
Offline ready: a script proves the game runs from the laptop with the venue's wifi off
Operator board: the arcade's back office, live, showing how agents build Piano Arcade
Operator replay: watch the build in 3D, one merge per note of Twinkle, on the piano
Options panel: one styled drawer for latency, effects and labels
Pause skin: a PAUSED menu, keyboard first, with a countdown that clicks
Pedal lamp: a sustain lamp in the HUD band, and Ped. marks under the bass staff on the sheet
Perf budget: frame time on the densest chart at 1920×1080, with fever and the stage on
Phone guard: a phone or tablet gets a 'made for a laptop or a piano' card instead of a broken highway
Prove a laptop can play to and read from the DGX-660
Piano out: replay your take on the piano, and a piano count-in
Piano sim: a virtual DGX-660 for testing the real MIDI path, and a /sim page
Piano voice: a chart names its GM voice and the DGX switches to it
Pill match: ghost outlines and note labels take their size from the note pills
Play slots: plugins add panels to the start and results screens, plus Pause and Quit
PROVISIONAL (learning lane): practice mode
Practice report: after the last chunk, the run's chunks, tries, hardest bars and time
Rank stamp: the rank letter stamps down
Record moment: NEW RECORD stamps in gold after the rank, with an arcade high-score entry
Records: best grades and a local top 5 with arcade initials
Replay view: watch your take on the highway while the piano plays it
Results layout: rank, tallies and a panel slot
Results tally: the counts tally up one by one
Rewind: in wait mode, ← moves back one bar and → skips ahead one, with the clock and holds set right
Scenes: scripted takes so every state can be seen, tested and filmed
Score card: Save card on the results downloads a PNG of the take
Score roll-up: the HUD score rolls to each new value, the multiplier flashes on tier-up
Music select layout: the song cards as an arcade music select
Select stage: the synthwave stage behind the music select
Select to stage: the focused jacket scales into the stage card
Sheet beams: beamed eighths and sixteenths, and beams and stems in their notes' judgment color
Sheet pickups: a pickup prints as a short bar 0, so the sheet's bar numbers match the printed score
Sheet review: from the results, open the score with this take's judgments already colored
Sheet view: the score in its own window, following a live take with judged noteheads
Sheet XML: a chart as MusicXML on a grand staff, for the sheet music window
Song card: one card per song for the music select
Song jacket: generated cover art for each song
Song options: Hands and Speed on the select's preview, remembered per song, passed to play and learn
Song pack 1: Ode to Joy, Chopin's Prelude Op. 28 No. 4 and Für Elise, with a MIDI-to-chart converter
Song pack 2: Gymnopédie, Clair de lune, Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2, Maple Leaf Rag and Moonlight's 3rd movement
Song palettes: each song's jacket palette tints the stage's sun and grid
Song preview: the highlighted song plays its opening in song select
Song requests: an agent turns a requested piece into a playable song
PROVISIONAL (learning lane): spike: turn a recording into a playable level
Song select: pick a piece from the library
Song sources: the song preview links each chart's public-domain score, the proof click
Song sweep: a bot plays every song and leaves a contact sheet of screenshots
Stage card: ARE YOU READY before the song
Static keyboard: one fixed C-to-C range per song, zoom off by default
Take graph: every note's timing over the song on the results screen
Take MIDI: download your take as a .mid file
Take store: every take saved to Supabase, with per-bar progress for the coach
Tempo curve: a rubato score beside the strict one
Timing feedback: how early or late you played, on the results screen
Twinkle 13: an agent writes Mozart's 13th variation, played on the DGX
UI sounds: cursor, confirm, back and a stage-card sting
UI tokens: the color and type tokens and the display font
Versus: two players on one piano
Versus scores: each half gets its own combo, score and multiplier in the HUD, and the higher score wins
Wait hands: learn one hand in wait mode while the other plays itself
Wait hint: after 3 s on a note, its key pulses, it sounds once and its name shows
Wait HUD: LEARN and note n / N instead of the score in wait mode
Wait mode: the highway waits for each note while you learn a song
Watch demo: W on the select plays the focused song with the perfect bot, labeled DEMO, then returns
Weak bars: accuracy per phrase, one click to practice the worst one
